title: LLM inference serving, Part 3: batching
tldr: How a server decides which requests share each forward pass, from static batches to continuous (iteration-level) batching: why one shared weight read makes batching the main lever, how static batching wastes about half its work on padding and waiting, Orca's iteration-level scheduling and selective batching, how vLLM v0.31.0's scheduler loop admits and retires requests every step under max_num_seqs and max_num_batched_tokens, what preemption does when the KV cache runs out, the throughput versus TPOT and TTFT trade-off with numbers, a step-through slot timeline, a batch trade-off calculator, a tested simulator, where the worker-pool analogy breaks, and an interview drill.
